body:
Resolve: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40460

Problem:
There is no shared utility for turning an filesystem-unsafe string into
a safe filename, so each subsystem makes its own encoding and plugins
reinvent the same wheel.

Solution:
add `vim.fs.slug()`, which generates a bounded, one-way filename from an
arbitrary string. An 8-char hash is always prepended for uniqueness.
A name that exceeds `opts.maxlen` becomes "{hash8}[-]{head}~~~{tail}".

comment_data.body:
🤔Interesting point. Could you explain more about why it's unsafe?

Although @justinmk proposed `…` back in the issue, I indeed thought about using `---`. But I still chose `…` in the end because we've used `-` to replace unsafe chars, thus using `---` here would cause ambiguity. `---` can be easily constructed, for example, `vim.fs.slug('foo - bar')` => `foo---bar`. And any other ASCII char is either unsafe or likely to be used in a file / path name.

I think it's a good idea to always append the `-{hash8}` to the end of the filename, regardless of how long it is, to prevent collisions (e.g. `file-name` vs. `file|name`; `/a/path` vs. `/a-path`, etc.), and also for consistency.

I noticed these while doing some simple tests, and just understood the behavior after reading the implementation:
```lua
-- returns "473a1d"
vim.fs.slug(('foo/bar/longlonglong.md'), {maxlen = 6})
-- `maxlen < 8` truncates the hash

-- returns "473a1da7"
vim.fs.slug(('foo/bar/longlonglong.md'), {maxlen = 12})
-- `8 < maxlen < 13` only returns the hash

--- `maxlen >= 13`, the tail and head start to appear gradually
-- "~~~d-473a1da7"
vim.fs.slug(('foo/bar/longlonglong.md'), {maxlen = 13})

-- "f~~~md-473a1da7"
vim.fs.slug(('foo/bar/longlonglong.md'), {maxlen = 15})
```
- Since we want to always add `-{hash8}`, we may want to reconsider the behavior of `maxlen`.
  e.g. enforce `maxlen` shoud be greater than 9 or refine the docs.
- Personally, I feel prioritizing head of the path (or even the filename) would make it more readable.
  e.g. `fo~473a1da7.md` or `lo~473a1da7.md`. I put the hash before the extension. This seems more natural and
  avoids having to consider reserved names. Although Windows can now create files like `NUL.txt` normally.
  Also, I'm not sure if the file extension is important here, or if we could just remove it.
- If we want the truncated name to preserve as many path components as possible, applying `pathshorten()` first
  might also be a good option. e.g. `b-lo~473a1da7.md` or `f-b-lo~473a1da7.md`
- I'm not sure whether we sould call `normalize` somewhere or state that this is the caller's responsibility.
  My concern is, if this is used for swapfiles later, I would expect paths like `foo/bar.md` and `foo\bar.md`
  to produce the same hash and name. Similar edge cases: `//?/C:/foo.md`, `//./C:/foo.md` and `C:/foo.md`, which
  all refer to the same file.
- If possible, could we also remove the leading `.-` similar to `system-escape --path`? This might make the generated
  filename safer to use.

My thoughts are still a bit scattered, not sure if I missed any ideas I had last night. These are just some ideas that came to mind, feel free to ignore them if they add too much complexity. :)
Not a fan of the hash before extension idea. I definitely think the hash should either be at the very start or the very end. Everything else is good and I agree with it.

@ntdiary @superatomic Thanks for your insightful ideas!


> * enforce `maxlen` shoud be greater than 9 or refine the docs.

This is definitely needed. Now `slug()` will check `opt.maxlen` and error if `maxlen < 8`. The threshold is 8 because the hash is 8 characters.


> * prioritizing head of the path (or even the filename) would make it more readable.

I put the hash at the very start so that if the path begins with `/` (common for `/home/...`), the leading `-` will be saved. And as a bonus, we don't need to handle win reserved names anymore. Also, will this possibly resolve your concern for the leading `.-`?


> * applying `pathshorten()` first might also be a good option

I added `opt.transform` to make it more customizable. It will be called before sanitization, and transform only the string without affecting the hash. Functions like `pathshorten()` and `normalize()` can be called here without changing the hash..


> * My concern is, if this is used for swapfiles later, I would expect paths like `foo/bar.md` and `foo\bar.md` to produce the same hash and name.

This is a real concern. `\` is now normalized to `/` before computing the hash.

> * I'm not sure whether we sould call `normalize` somewhere or state that this is the caller's responsibility.

The only built-in normalization is `\` -> `/` (minimal and universal). Anything beyond that, like `vim.fs.normalize()`, prefix stripping, etc. , is up to the caller. Doing it beforehand affects the hash; using `opts.transform` does not.

> * Similar edge cases: `//?/C:/foo.md`, `//./C:/foo.md` and `C:/foo.md`, which all refer to the same file.

I think it is the caller's responsibility. `\` → `/` is about separators, but NT namespace prefixes are more specialized and I'd rather not add implicit behavior for them.

> * Also, I'm not sure if the file extension is important here, or if we could just remove it.

The extensions now can be stripped by `opt.transform` and doing so won't cause collision because the full input (including the extension) still determines the hash.

I thought this over a bit more, and I think `vim.fs.slug()` should be rather opinionated. For this reason, I think `opts.transform` should be dropped, and also probably `opts.map` as well. Instead of leaving these up to the caller, we should just decide a "correct" way to do it, that way Nvim core and every plugin have the same consistent syntax.

Additionally, `vim.fs.normalize()` should be built in. This will handle a lot of edge-cases "for free" and will make calling `vim.fs.slug()` have less footguns.

regarding `maxlen` default: it should be less than 255, since usually these paths live in `stdpath()`, which is already somewhat deep...

> I put the hash at the very start so that if the path begins with `/` (common for `/home/...`), the leading `-` will be saved.

leading `-` works on all filesystems, what's the problem? hash at the start means that sorting doesn't work, that's a big cost.

anyways, i think we can drop the leading `-` :  just assume/enforce that all paths are ALWAYS absolute. 

UNC paths like `//foo` will have a singe leading `-`: `-foo`. Or for readability, that may be a strong case for a special thing like `=unc-`.

> The only built-in normalization is `\` -> `/` (minimal and universal). Anything beyond that, like `vim.fs.normalize()`, prefix stripping, etc. , is up to the caller

why? slugs should not have "duplicates", so normalization is an inherent requirement, thus it should always `normalize()`. it looks like this was already resolved though 👍 

caller can "transform" the string themselves so I don't see a need for `transform` either 👍

> regarding `maxlen` default: it should be less than 255, since usually these paths live in `stdpath()`, which is already somewhat deep...

The 255 limit is per path sep limit, at least on Unix, so it can be exactly 255. AFAIK this is the same on Windows too.

Perhaps it should be slightly less than 255 so callers can safely add their own file extensions afterwards, like `.swp`? I think it should still be exactly 255 for clarity, but it's worth considering.

> leading `-` works on all filesystems, what's the problem?

The problem is that the leading `-` looks ugly (imo). `systemd-escape --path` drops the leading `-` for this reason.

> hash at the start means that sorting doesn't work, that's a big cost.

Yeah, that's fair. We should probably move it to the end again and just drop the leading `-` separately.

> The 255 limit is per path sep limit, at least on Unix, so it can be exactly 255. AFAIK this is the same on Windows too.

on Windows by default the entire path is still limited to 255. anyways, even if the limit was infinite, these slugs are intended to be useful and readable, not infinite.

> leading `-` works on all filesystems, what's the problem? This is no problem. I'm just saying we can reuse the `-` here. And putting hash at the end of filename could miss the extension. So, if there is no objection, ti would be `{head}~~~{tail}-{hash8}{ext}`. > caller can "transform" the string themselves so I don't see a need for `transform` either 👍
The intention of adding opt.transform (click to expand) Well, I think I need to explain it a little bit. The intention of adding `opt.transform`: Take `/home/foo/bar/example.md` for example. Let: ``` hash_a = hash8("/home/foo/bar/example.md") hash_b = hash8(vim.fn.pathshorten("/home/foo/bar/example.md")) ``` Then: ```md vim.fs.slug("/home/foo/bar/example.md") -> {hash_a}-home-foo-bar-example.md vim.fs.slug(vim.fn.pathshorten("/home/foo/bar/example.md")) -> {hash_b}-h-f-b-example.md <--- ^ ^ vim.fs.slug(vim.fn.pathshorten("/home/fff/bbb/example.md")) -> {hash_b}-h-f-b-example.md <--- ^ ^ ``` Thus, different paths have the same `slug()` result. But ``` vim.fs.slug("/home/foo/bar/example.md", { transform = vim.fn.pathshorten }) -> {**hash_a**}-h-f-b-example.md ``` It allows the caller to manipulate the result string _without changing hash_ / causing collisions. And why can't the caller manipulate after `slug()` -- I think that's a bit annoying for callers to do string manipulation. I dropped this only because I do agree that we should be "opinionated" and this use case is unlikely to occur(?). Not sure if this is "over-design".
> regarding `maxlen` default: it should be less than 255, since usually these paths live in `stdpath()`, which is already somewhat deep... I thought it's a good idea to let the caller to decide. But providing a safe default value is also good. How about 180?

> This is no problem. I'm just saying we can reuse the `-` here. And putting hash at the end of filename could miss the extension.
> So, if there is no objection, ti would be `{head}~~~{tail}-{hash8}{ext}`.

Hash should be at the very end; don't do anything special with the file extension (it's just part of the tail). The extension isn't relevant anyway; e.g. the file format for the undofile of `README.md` is binary, not markdown.

> I thought it's a good idea to let the caller to decide. But providing a safe default value is also good. How about 180?

180 default sounds good to me!

> And why can't the caller manipulate after `slug()` -- I think that's a bit annoying for callers to do string manipulation.

makes sense, but should wait until someone has an actual use-case. plus they can do surgery on the slug() result already.
